title: Smooth geometric stalks and coordinate-section closed fibres
statement:
Let $f:V\to S$ be smooth between locally Noetherian schemes. For compatible geometric points
$\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ with
$\bar v$ over $\bar s$, put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ and
$B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar v}$. Use the canonical local ring map
$\varphi:A\to B$ induced by `strictHenselizationMap` and put
$\mathfrak m_A=\operatorname{maximalIdeal}(A)$ and
$\mathfrak m_B=\operatorname{maximalIdeal}(B)$. Then $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings,
$\varphi$ is flat and local, and $B/\mathfrak m_A B$ is regular. For every ideal
$I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, the canonical quotient map $A/I\to B/IB$ is flat and local,
and its closed fibre is canonically $B/(IB+\mathfrak m_A B)\simeq B/\mathfrak m_A B$.

In the affine-space case, supply an isomorphism over $S$,
$e:V\simeq\mathbf A(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin} r))_S$. For a finite subset
$K$ of the coordinate indices, let $t_i\in B$ be the image of
`AffineSpace.coord` under $\Gamma$ of the structural map followed by $e$. If
$t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ for $i\in K$, then for every $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ the ring
$B/(IB+(t_i:i\in K))$ is Noetherian and local, its canonical map from $A/I$ is flat,
and its closed fibre is $F_K=B/(\mathfrak m_A B+(t_i:i\in K))$, which is regular; moreover
$\dim(B/\mathfrak m_A B)=\dim F_K+|K|$.

proof.text: Use the smooth strict-local base model to obtain Noetherianity of both strict local rings and the flat ordinary map A to C. Convert its specified pointed-etale cocone to IsStrictHenselization and then to the triples presentation. Faithful flatness of the triples colimit makes C to H flat; compose and transport through the model ring equivalence B to H. The base model gives locality. Naturality of the Gamma-Spec isomorphisms identifies the model map Spec.preimage(strictHenselizationMap) with the displayed Gamma-defined map.

proof.text: The closed-fibre model gives the evaluation-kernel equality and a ring equivalence from B/m_A B to a regular local strict geometric stalk. Regular-local localization implies that the stalk is a regular ring; transport regularity back through the equivalence.

source.place: Assembly of the four model lemmas; Tags 00HI, 04GU, 04GW, 05WS, 06LK and 06LN.

proof.text: For I contained in m_A, use the quotient-tensor ring equivalence and flat base change to make A/I to B/IB flat. Locality descends by lifting quotient representatives and reflecting units through the local quotient map. The extended ideal IB lies in m_B, so the quotient is nonzero local. Since IB is contained in m_A B, their supremum is m_A B; quotEquivOfEq gives the displayed fibre isomorphism, fixing each class.

source.place: Assembly of the four model lemmas; Tags 00HI, 04GU, 04GW, 05WS, 06LK and 06LN.

proof.text: For the coordinate subspace use the affine-coordinate model. Its explicit zero-insertion map has composite with the ambient projection equal to the complementary affine-space projection, which the model states is smooth. Apply the flat strict-local construction from step 1 to that projection. Uniqueness of pointed strict-henselization maps proves composition with the zero-insertion ring map; the quotientIso_map equation therefore identifies the resulting flat map with A to B/J_K. Apply quotient flat base change and the double-quotient isomorphism to obtain A/I to B/(IB+J_K). Noetherianity descends from B, and both summands lie in m_B, giving locality. The equality (IB+J_K)+m_A B=m_A B+J_K gives the class-preserving fibre isomorphism.

source.place: Assembly of the four model lemmas; Tags 00HI, 04GU, 04GW, 05WS, 06LK and 06LN.

proof.text: Take the two polynomial presentations supplied by the affine-coordinate model. The quotient-induced residue-field map is bijective, so transport the first residue-field action to the second chosen separable closure. Separability transfers along the residue-field ring equivalence; IsSepClosure.equiv identifies the two closures. Reindexing the pointed-etale diagram by the equivalence of over categories preserves its colimit and its algebra identification, giving the first model with the same closure as the second. Apply the stated polynomial strict-local coordinate dimension lemma. Transport its dimension equality through iso0 and iso1; regular-local localization and iso1 give the required regular ring. This works for empty and full K and arbitrary polynomial primes.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $v:V\to S$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Choose a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$ and its image $\bar s$ in $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O_{S,\bar s}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}$ be the strict local rings, namely the geometric stalks of the etale structure sheaves [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Then $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings and $A\to B$ is a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The closed fibre $F=B/\mathfrak m_A B$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, the map $A/I\to B/IB$ is flat and local, and has the same closed fibre $F$.

There is also the following coordinate form. Suppose $V=\mathbf A^r_S$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], with coordinates $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, and let $K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ be any subset for which $t_i\in\mathfrak m_B$ for all $i\in K$. Put $k=|K|$. Then for every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ the ring $B/(IB+(t_i:i\in K))$ is Noetherian and local, its map from $A/I$ is flat, and its closed fibre is $F_K=F/(\bar t_i:i\in K)$. Moreover $F_K$ is regular and
$$\dim F=\dim F_K+k,$$
where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].
